subject: Air-gapped deployment: maintenance windows, operator scenarios, and SLA responsibilities
messages:
From: Starlake Health Procurement <procurement@starlake.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-12-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Air-gapped deployment: maintenance & patching responsibilities

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the detailed RFP response so far. A couple of follow-ups from procurement and our security team before we proceed to contract: can you provide a clear ownership matrix for day-to-day maintenance, emergency patching, and rollback responsibilities for a fully air-gapped/private deployment? Specifically: who owns scheduling maintenance windows, who performs operator-level interventions (customer ops vs Redwood TAM), how are hotfixes delivered when there is no outbound egress, and what SLA/response times do you commit for security-critical incidents that require an immediate patch?

We're also interested in an example maintenance cadence (monthly vs quarterly), what types of changes require a scheduled window, and what falls under out-of-band emergency actions. It would be helpful to receive a short operations playbook and a sample maintenance schedule spreadsheet.

Can you get that to us by the end of next week? Procurement is coordinating internal approvals and needs this to finalize the SOW.

Thanks,
Oliver Hartley
Director, Procurement
Starlake Health

Attachment: none
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Oliver Hartley <ohartley@starlake.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-12-01T12:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Air-gapped deployment: maintenance & patching responsibilities

Oliver —

Appreciate the clear ask. High level answers up front, followed by an attached matrix and a sample maintenance schedule (attached). Marissa and Ben are looped in for the technical runbook and operations details.

Summary (high level):
- Maintenance scheduling: Customer-owned (Starlake) for non-critical changes; Redwood recommends two maintenance windows per quarter but will defer to your calendar.
- Emergency security patches: Redwood provides packaging and validated patch bundles. For air-gapped installs we support delivery via secure courier (signed artifacts) and guided on-site or remote operator application. Redwood will commit to an initial acknowledgement within 1 hour (business hours) and a remediation plan within 8 hours for critical CVEs when we have a validated patch available.
- Operator interventions: Day-to-day L2 tasks are customer-run; Redwood provides operator runbooks and can provide a named TAM or on-call engineer to be an authorized operator for escalations under a separate support addendum.
- Rollback: Rollback procedures are part of the operator runbook; we provide snapshot and rollback guidance but do not assume control of customer-backedup state unless covered by a managed-ops contract.

See attached: maintenance_schedule.xlsx (sample cadence and blocking windows) and a short ownership matrix. We'll follow up with the detailed runbook and emergency playbook today.

Next steps we propose:
1) Marissa to share the operator runbook and emergency playbook.
2) Ben to outline the signed-patch delivery process and courier options.
3) Schedule a 30-minute call to lock in the maintenance SLA language for the SOW.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachment: maintenance_schedule.xlsx (stub)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, Oliver Hartley <ohartley@starlake.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-12-02T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Air-gapped deployment: maintenance & patching responsibilities

Oliver / Vanessa / Ben —

Attached are the two items we discussed: operator_runbook.md (concise step-by-step operator checklist for common L2 tasks, pre/post-maintenance verification steps, and rollback commands) and emergency_playbook.pdf (escalation decision tree, validation checklist for security fixes, and sample communication templates). Highlights below:

Operator runbook highlights:
- Pre-maintenance: take model and config snapshots, validate KV cache snapshot, export metrics window (last 72 hrs)
- Apply maintenance: staged sequence (orchestrator stop -> apply kernel/quantization patch -> restart serving runtime -> smoke tests)
- Post-maintenance validation: throughput sanity check, latency p99 step, sample prompt validation, and integration smoke tests
- Rollback: revert to snapshot, clear KV cache, rehydrate model artifacts, verify keys and signatures

Emergency playbook highlights:
- Classification: Critical (executes out-of-band) vs Standard (scheduled)
- Critical response target: acknowledgment in 1 hour (24x7), plan within 8 hours, patch delivery window variable depending on courier/airgap logistics
- Patch verification: signed bundle, checksums, signed manifest, hash verification step in runbook

Delivery options for patch bundles (air-gapped):
1) Secure courier with signed SSD (customer receives and applies)
2) On-site Redwood engineer under supervised access (if covered in contract)
3) Transfer via approved removable media and verification steps in runbook

I've included conservative time estimates for logistics in the attached operator_runbook.md and the sample maintenance_schedule.xlsx included earlier.

Attachments: operator_runbook.md, emergency_playbook.pdf (stubs)
From: Oliver Hartley <ohartley@starlake.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-12-06T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Air-gapped deployment: maintenance & patching responsibilities

Thanks — a few clarifying points from our security team:
1) The 1-hour acknowledgement window: does that apply 24x7 for Critical classification, or only during business hours?
2) For the signed bundle delivery, can Redwood guarantee cryptographic signing with customer-provided keys (we need remote verification without exposing vendor keys)?
3) If we need an on-site Redwood engineer to perform the operation, what is the maximum lead time and cost model?
4) For rollback, can Redwood provide an example of a rollback verification checklist we can include in the SOW?

If you can answer those four bullets in a short update we'll share with our security and procurement teams and then we can formalize the SOW language.

Oliver

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Oliver Hartley <ohartley@starlake.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-12-08T14:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Air-gapped deployment: maintenance & patching responsibilities

Oliver — quick answers inline to keep this short: 

1) Acknowledgement window: Critical = 24x7 acknowledgment within 1 hour. We operate a 24x7 on-call rotation for security-critical incidents.

2) Cryptographic signing: Yes — we can sign patch bundles with our key and include a process to accept and register a Starlake public key for verification. The runbook includes the hash and signature verification steps so your operators can verify bundles before applying.

3) On-site engineer: we support on-site engagements under the Private deployment addendum. Typical lead time is 3-10 business days depending on region/clearance; we can offer an accelerated (48-72 hour) option as a billable service. We will include a standard rate card in the SOW.

4) Rollback checklist: included in operator_runbook.md but I can summarize: verify snapshot integrity, stop incoming traffic, restore artifact, run smoke tests, validate model outputs against golden prompts, then declare service back. We'll provide a one-page checklist suitable for the SOW.

Attached: signed_patch_process.pdf (detailed courier and signing steps)

Ben Carter
Technical Account Manager
Redwood Inference
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Oliver Hartley <ohartley@starlake.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-12-14T15:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Air-gapped deployment: maintenance & patching responsibilities

Oliver —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the clarifying questions. Confirming acceptance of the responses below and proposing next steps so procurement can finalize the SOW:

- Acknowledgement SLA: Critical incidents = 24x7 acknowledgement <= 1 hour (we will add this as SLA language).
- Signing: Redwood will provide signed patch bundles and support registering a Starlake public key for verification; verification steps will be included in the runbook.
- On-site: we will include an optional on-site engineer line item with standard and accelerated lead times (3-10 business days / 48-72hr accelerated) and a preliminary rate card.
- Rollback checklist: we'll provide a one-page checklist for the SOW; the operator_runbook.md already contains the full procedure.

Please review the attached items and accept the DocuSign statement of work when ready (link below). If accepted, we suggest scheduling a 30-minute kickoff the week of Dec 20 to align on maintenance windows and to capture the contact details for the named TAM and your security ops contact.

Best,
